# FlareDispatch

> BYOC CI/CD that moves the expensive half of GitHub Actions onto a Cloudflare stack you own —
> Workflows for orchestration, Containers for execution, Browser Rendering for e2e, R2 for cache and
> artifacts. Runs are typed Effect-TS programs, not YAML. The **substrate** is its execution
> environment for agentic work: containers under deny-all egress, ticket-gated admission, artifacts
> on R2, metered model access — consumed only through a service-binding facade.

Paths are relative to the repository root of `fractalboxdev/flare-dispatch`. Everything below is
markdown; nothing requires running a build to read.

## Substrate — consumer guides

- [Consuming the facade](apps/docs/substrate/facade.md): how to bind, the call sequence, admission
  modes, idempotency, and how every failure arrives as a typed refusal.
- [Facade API reference](apps/docs/reference/substrate-contract/README.md): every exported type,
  generated by TypeDoc from `packages/substrate-contract` and regenerated in CI.
- [Contract versioning policy](apps/docs/substrate/contract-versioning.md): what bumps
  `CONTRACT_VERSION`, why output unions are breaking and input unions are not, and what a consumer
  migration costs.

## Substrate — maintainer and operator guides

- [Authoring a grant profile](apps/docs/substrate/grant-profiles.md): how egress is granted, the three
  properties every profile holds, the review checklist, graduation `legacy → report → enforce`, and
  the position on operator-authored profiles.
- [BYOC upgrade runbook](apps/docs/substrate/byoc-upgrade.md): provisioning, the operator overlay,
  deploy order, `/health` verification, version floors, and rollback cost.

## Design records

- [Platform spec](apps/substrate/specs/platform.md): boundary, security floor, tenancy, adoption plan.
- [ADR index](apps/substrate/specs/adr/README.md): one record per settled decision, with the evidence
  that produced it. The platform spec states what; the ADRs carry why; the guides above state how.

## Optional

- [Repository overview](README.md): what FlareDispatch is and how a consumer repo offloads a job.
- [Agent conventions](AGENTS.md): architecture, component mapping, and the conventions this repo is
  written to.
